title: Hit-conditioned behavior audit and canary runbook for KV/prefix cache changes
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: Recent internal incidents and several small regressions suggest cache hits (KV/prefix) can change model outputs in subtle but customer-visible ways. This ticket builds an audit harness that (a) quantifies hit-conditioned behavioral deltas across model/config changes, (b) produces an automated canary runbook and gating rules, and (c) integrates signal into the Console and rollout automation. The goal is to reduce silent output drift caused by cache semantics and make rollouts safe by default.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New 'hit_signature' metric computed per-request and exposed in per-route dashboards.
2) Synthetic perturbation harness that runs on every canary and returns: embedding-cosine delta, response edit-distance, and a calibrated 'semantic-regression' score.
3) Canary runbook implemented with stepwise traffic ramp (0->5->20->100) and automatic rollback if semantic-regression > 0.04 or human-fail-rate > 2% on seeded probes.
4) Playbook docs + on-call checklist added to Confluence and linked from rollout UI.
tasks: Design metric set and thresholds with SRE/Applied-ML (Aisha)
Implement hit_signature: (cache_key, kv_length, prefix_hash, hit_location) + lightweight fingerprint (Marco)
Build synthetic perturbation harness: corpus selection, paraphrase/noise generators, and ground-truth anchors (Applied-ML)
Add embedding-based delta pipeline (Cosine + bootstrap CI) to metrics service (Observability)
Add canary automation rules: gating thresholds, progressive ramping stages, and automatic fallback
Wire metric to Console: route-level signal and per-canary report (Frontend)
Smoke test on internal staging with 200 seeded prompts and run full harness on canary release
